[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Middleware Architecture and Execution Order in Django"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Django middleware is a framework of hooks into Django\'s request/response processing. It is a lightweight, low-level plugin system that globally alters Django\'s input or output. Understanding how middleware executes is crucial for handling authentication, session management, security enhancements, and request logging."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"The Anatomy of Django Middleware"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Django middleware is simply a callable that takes a get_response callable and returns a callable. It can be written as a function or as a class. When Django initializes, it processes the MIDDLEWARE setting from settings.py from top to bottom."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"class SimpleMiddleware:
    def __init__(self, get_response):
        self.get_response = get_response

    def __call__(self, request):
        # Code executed for each request before
        # the view (and later middleware) are called.

        response = self.get_response(request)

        # Code executed for each request after
        # the view is called.

        return response"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"The Onion Model of Execution Order"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Think of Django middleware as an onion. The incoming request starts at the outermost layer, peeling inward through every middleware until it reaches the view. Once the view generates a response, the response travels outward in reverse order, passing through the same middleware components again."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Request Phase: Executed top-to-bottom as listed in settings.MIDDLEWARE."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"View Phase: Reached after all request phases complete, triggering the specific view handler."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Response Phase: Executed bottom-to-top in reverse order of settings.MIDDLEWARE."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Visualizing Execution Flow"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"Request -> Middleware A (Before) -> Middleware B (Before) -> View
Response <- Middleware A (After)  <- Middleware B (After)  <- View"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Writing Custom Middleware"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Let us implement a custom logging middleware that tracks the total processing time of an HTTP request. We will inject a header into the response object during the outward journey."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"import time
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

class RequestTimingMiddleware:
    def __init__(self, get_response):
        self.get_response = get_response

    def __call__(self, request):
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Process request downstream
        response = self.get_response(request)
        
        duration = time.time() - start_time
        response["X-Page-Execution-Time"] = str(duration)
        
        logger.info(f"Path: {request.path} took {duration:.4f} seconds")
        return response"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Registering Middleware"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"To activate your custom middleware, add its dotted Python path to the MIDDLEWARE list inside your project\'s settings.py file. Placement matters significantly based on whether your middleware depends on session or authentication states."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"MIDDLEWARE = [
    "django.middleware.security.SecurityMiddleware",
    "django.contrib.sessions.middleware.SessionMiddleware",
    "django.middleware.common.CommonMiddleware",
    "django.middleware.csrf.CsrfViewMiddleware",
    "django.contrib.auth.middleware.AuthenticationMiddleware",
    "django.contrib.messages.middleware.MessageMiddleware",
    "django.middleware.clickjacking.XFrameOptionsMiddleware",
    "myapp.middleware.RequestTimingMiddleware", # Placed last to measure total time
]"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Keep middleware lightweight to prevent compounding latency on every single HTTP request."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Handle exceptions gracefully or allow Django\'s exception middleware to catch them further up the stack."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Be mindful of execution order dependencies. For example, AuthenticationMiddleware requires SessionMiddleware to run beforehand."}]
